title: Ramakant Kanaugiya @ Vinod Kanaugiya v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta and Prashant Kumar, JJ.
disposition: Disposed; theft recovery withdrawn; fresh Supply Code order after hearing.
headnote: A writ against a theft-recovery notice is disposed of when the electricity department withdraws the demand and undertakes to pass a fresh order after hearing, strictly in accordance with the procedure under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court does not examine the demand.
facts: Ramakant Kanaugiya alias Vinod Kanaugiya filed Writ-C No. 5215 of 2023 in the Allahabad High Court against the State of U.P. and the electricity department, challenging a demand notice dated 27 December 2022 for recovery of Rs. 77,691 for alleged theft of electricity. The Bench adjourned the matter on 15 February 2023 to show the department's counsel and, on 21 February 2023, granted three days for instructions. On 27 February 2023 counsel stated that the impugned recovery had been withdrawn and that a fresh order would follow after hearing.

holding_units.topic: Disposal on withdrawal of a theft-recovery notice
holding_units.holding: Once the licensee withdraws the impugned theft recovery and states that a fresh order will be passed after hearing the consumer, the writ is disposed of with liberty to pass that order strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, without the Court deciding the demand.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench recorded the department's withdrawal of the Rs. 77,691 theft recovery and disposed of the writ, reserving a fresh order after hearing under the Supply Code, without construing any clause.

not_decided.point: Whether any sum is recoverable from the petitioner for the alleged theft of electricity
not_decided.note: Left to a fresh order after opportunity of hearing, strictly in accordance with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
